analogy.rationale: Glycine receptors are ligand-gated chloride channels with limited expression in these cell lines, so antagonists produce little transcriptional response; the closest analogs are other ionotropic inhibitory neurotransmitter receptor antagonists (GABA, nicotinic/muscarinic acetylcholine) that also act on poorly expressed neuronal receptors, with chloride channel blockers sharing the downstream chloride conductance mechanism.
